preamble: Deretroflexion of the retroflex ejective affricate [ʈʂʼ] to the palato-alveolar [t͡ʃʼ], merging the two ejective affricates. In the Shapsug and Natukhai dialects of Adyghe (West Circassian) the retroflex affricates чъ [ʈʂ] and чӏ [ʈʂʼ], which Chemguy (Temirgoy) and Bzhedug keep, merged with ч [t͡ʃ] and кӏ [t͡ʃʼ] (Wikipedia, Shapsug dialect, citing Kerasheva 1957: 28–29). Wikipedia's Proto-Circassian article likewise gives t͡ʃʼ as the Shapsug reflex of Proto-Circassian *t͡ʂʼ, and Wiktionary has Shapsug гъукӏы (ʁʷət͡ʃʼə) beside literary and Bzhedug Adyghe гъучӏы (ʁʷət͡ʂʼə) 'iron'. Standard Kabardian instead turned both ejective affricates into the fricative ɕʼ. In Kartvelian, Wiktionary reconstructs a Proto-Kartvelian ejective *c̣₁ (subscript-1 series) whose reflex is č̣ (ჭ) in Laz, Mingrelian and Svan but c̣ (წ) in Georgian: *mc̣₁er- 'fly' gives Mingrelian ჭანდი č̣andi and Laz მჭაჯი beside Old Georgian მწერი mc̣eri. Wikipedia's Proto-Kartvelian consonant table, citing Gamkrelidze (1966: 70) and Fähnrich (2002: 5), gives *c̣₁ the value [t͡ʂʼ], distinct from *c̣ [t͡sʼ] and *č̣ [t͡ʃʼ]. The retroflex value belongs to that reconstruction; the cognates themselves show only the correspondence of Zan and Svan č̣ to Georgian c̣.
